Schizaeaceae.key_door: specialized fertile pinnae/lobes with subapical-annulus sporangia; Anemia = erect modified basal fertile pinnae, Lygodium = climbing indeterminate rachis with fertile fringes

Ophioglossaceae.key_door: single frond divided into sterile trophophore + fertile sporophore with large annulus-free eusporangia

anchor_families.Pteridaceae: Joey Santore Adiantum capillus-veneris fertile-frond/pseudoindusium frame used as preferred private-study comparison
anchor_families.Polypodiaceae: ordinary round sori on blade surface comparison

joey_private_anchor.policy: preferred private-study comparison asset; public reuse remains separate

taxonomy_notes: Current Kew Schizaeaceae includes Anemia and Lygodium; older FNA Anemiaceae and Lygodiaceae treatments are preserved as morphology/search provenance.
Anemia mexicana is accepted and native from west-central Texas southward.
Lygodium japonicum is accepted but introduced in Texas.
Current Kew treats Sceptridium as a synonym of Botrychium; source Sceptridium biternatum maps to current Botrychium biternatum.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Do not create separate project families for older Anemiaceae or Lygodiaceae.
Do not keep Sceptridium biternatum as a duplicate current species alongside Botrychium biternatum.
Use Joey Adiantum only as the Pteridaceae comparison anchor; it does not establish Schizaeaceae/Ophioglossaceae taxonomy or range.
